# TypeScript API

Reactive routes work without any TypeScript. Write some only when you need side effects beyond patching the
DOM — showing a validation message, reacting to connection loss, driving a custom widget.

## The generated client

Every reactive route gets a generated `__ssr_gen__.ts` next to its `index.html`:

```typescript
// Code generated by github.com/sergei-svistunov/go-ssr. DO NOT EDIT.
import { createSsrClient } from 'gossr-runtime';
import 'gossr-runtime/ssr-block.css';

export type ReadVars = {
  displayName: string;
  visitorsOnline: number;
}

export type WriteVars = {
  displayName: string;
}

export const ssr = createSsrClient<ReadVars, WriteVars>({ … });
```

`ReadVars` mirrors every reactive variable in the route with its Go type mapped to TypeScript; `WriteVars` is
the `client-writable` subset. The WebSocket URL and route key are filled in by the generator.

The webpack plugin bundles `__ssr_gen__.ts` into the route's chunk whether or not you write an `index.ts`, so
the connection is established on every reactive route automatically.

## Using it

```typescript
import { ssr } from './__ssr_gen__';
```

| Call | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ssr.get(name)` | last received rendered HTML for a binding, or `undefined` |
| `ssr.set(name, value)` | write a value to the server; only accepts `client-writable` names |
| `ssr.on(name, cb)` | run `cb(html)` when a patch for that variable arrives |
| `ssr.onError(cb)` | `cb(varName, message)` when the server rejects a write |
| `ssr.onConnect(cb)` | connection established or re-established |
| `ssr.onDisconnect(cb)` | `cb(code, reason)` when an established connection drops unexpectedly |
| `ssr.onConnectError(cb)` | `cb(status)` when the initial upgrade request is rejected |

Every subscription function returns an unsubscribe function.

Note what `get` and `on` deal in: the **rendered HTML string** for a binding site, not the Go value. The
runtime has already applied it to the DOM by the time your callback runs, so use these for side effects rather
than for rendering.

```typescript
const errorEl = document.getElementById('display-name-error');

ssr.onError((varName, message) => {
    if (varName === 'displayName' && errorEl) {
        errorEl.textContent = message;
    }
});

ssr.on('displayName', () => {
    if (errorEl) errorEl.textContent = '';
});
```

`ssr.set` is fire and forget. The value comes back as a normal patch once the server has validated it, so do
not treat a `set` call as having taken effect until then:

```typescript
ssr.set('displayName', 'Ada');
```

Calling `set` with a name that is not in `WriteVars` is a TypeScript compile error, which is the point of the
generated types.

## Connection state

```typescript
ssr.onDisconnect((code, reason) => banner.hidden = false);
ssr.onConnect(() => banner.hidden = true);
```

`onDisconnect` does not fire on normal navigation away from the page. Reconnection with backoff is automatic;
after it succeeds the server sends a fresh init frame with every current value, so the page does not need
reloading.

## Packages and configuration

```json
{
  "dependencies": { "gossr-runtime": "^0.1.0" },
  "devDependencies": { "gossr-assets-webpack-plugin": "^0.1.1" }
}
```

- **`gossr-runtime`** — the client: WebSocket handling, the shared-connection multiplexer, the DOM patcher and
  the `ssr` object. Also ships `gossr-runtime/ssr-block.css`, which the generated file imports so wrapper
  elements do not affect layout.
- **`gossr-assets-webpack-plugin`** — emits `webpack-assets.json` for the generator and copies images into the
  static output.

`tsconfig.json` needs `"moduleResolution": "bundler"` or `"nodenext"` so the runtime's `exports` map is
honoured.

## Per-route entry points

`index.ts` and `styles.scss` next to a template are bundled into that route's chunk and loaded by
`<ssr:assets/>`. A parent route's chunk loads on every page beneath it, so shared behaviour belongs in the
layout's `index.ts` and page-specific behaviour in the page's own.
